If the destroy request fails, the promise rejects silently: the row is never removed via sendAction('deleteHost') and no error message is shown to the admin. The mechanism is directly verifiable from the diff — the asymmetric error handling between save and delete in the same component is concrete.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save()`, which explicitly does). If the server delete fails (network error/validation/500), the promise rejection is unhandled and no admin-facing error is shown. Also, since `deleteHost` is only sent inside the `then`, the row will remain, but without feedback about why deletion failed—matching the finding.
